tools.description: Aligns one or more objects along a specified edge or center axis. Objects can be aligned relative to each other (selection bounding box) or to the active artboard. Alignment is single-axis: 'left'/'center'/'right' shift X only (Y unchanged); 'top'/'middle'/'bottom' shift Y only (X unchanged). Prefer this tool over manual MoveObjects calculations whenever you need to align edges or centers of multiple objects.

relativeTo.description: Reference frame: 'selection' (bounding box of all objects) or 'artboard' (active artboard bounds).

uuids.description: Array of UUIDs of objects to align (minimum 1 when aligning to artboard, minimum 2 when aligning to selection). Layer UUIDs are not supported. IMPORTANT: pass as a native JSON array, not a stringified array.

tools.name: AlignObjects

tools.description: ALWAYS use this tool instead of manual MoveObjects offset math to CREATE or ADJUST equal gaps between 2+ objects — including improving/fixing/adjusting uniform tracking or letter-spacing in a wordmark/logotype/word made of separate letter objects. Not for pure repositioning of an already-spaced group (use MoveObjects instead, which preserves existing spacing). Only supports one uniform gap value for all objects, not unequal/proportional/ratio-based spacing (e.g. non-uniform kerning between specific letter pairs). Distributes objects evenly along an axis. If spacing is provided, objects are placed with that exact gap between them (2+ objects). If spacing is omitted, objects are distributed evenly within the total span from first to last (3+ objects required — pass explicit spacing instead for exactly 2 objects).

spacing.description: Explicit gap in points between objects. Omit to distribute evenly within current span.

uuids.description: Array of UUIDs of objects to distribute (minimum 3 for even distribution, 2 for explicit spacing). Layer UUIDs are not supported. IMPORTANT: pass as a native JSON array, not a stringified array.

tools.name: DistributeObjects

tools.description: Sets visual appearance and state properties (fill, stroke, opacity, blend mode, locked, hidden, overprint) on one or more objects in a single call. All properties are optional — only provided properties are changed. To remove fill or stroke, set fillColor='none' or strokeColor='none'. Supports batch operations via uuids array. fillColor/strokeColor overwrite the entire fill/stroke of the objects you name with one literal color, applied exactly — use this tool to set a literal target color or color space (e.g. a hex, a Pantone/spot name, or grayscale/'black and white') on objects whose UUIDs you already know. To apply one flat color to a set you must first find — by criteria (e.g. 'change all red shapes to blue') or every object (e.g. 'make the whole illustration blue') — prefer FindObjects' setProperties when available. For 'grayscale'/'black and white' on multi-colored artwork, don't apply one flat gray to everything (that flattens the tonal variation) — read each object's current color via GetVisualAppearance, derive a gray from its luminance, and call once per distinct gray with the matching uuids. For an open-ended palette/theme/mood change with no fixed target color ('make it warmer', 'recolor to autumn', 'reduce to 2 colors'), use RecolorArtwork instead. NOTE: This tool handles flat colors only. For gradient fills or strokes — or to change angle, stops, or type on an existing gradient — use SetGradient instead. Providing a flat fillColor on an object with a gradient fill will replace the gradient with a flat color. Never invent, guess, or autocomplete swatch names. Text frames: fill/stroke color, paint toggles, overprint, and stroke-style properties apply to characters via the text engine; opacity and blend mode behavior is unchanged. IMPORTANT: Set locked=false or hidden=false ONLY when the user explicitly asks to unlock/show objects or explicitly references locked/hidden state (e.g., 'unlock layer X', 'show the hidden group', 'delete the locked layer'). Generic requests like 'delete all', 'move everything', 'rotate the shapes', or 'place/add X in layer Y' do NOT grant permission to unlock/unhide first, even if that's the only way to fulfill the request — ask the user instead. When a requested fill/stroke/paint change can't be applied to an object's type, that object is reported in skipped_objects (with skipped_count and a per-object reason), NOT failed_objects; opacity, blend mode, locked, and hidden still apply. Symbol instances are the common case — the response additionally carries a symbol_link_guidance field explaining the symbol link must be broken first. Response shape: {success, details, success_count, fail_count, failed_objects?, skipped_count, skipped_objects?, symbol_link_guidance?}.

blendMode.description: Blend mode. Omit to leave unchanged.

fillColor.description: Fill color. Hex '#RRGGBB', a named document swatch via {\"model\":\"swatch\",\"name\":\"PANTONE 485 C\"}, or a color object (for example {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0.15,\"m\":0.7,\"y\":0.35,\"k\":0.05}). Use 'none' to remove fill. Omit for no change. For object models rgb/cmyk/gray, prefer normalized channels in [0,1] (for example {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":0.25,\"g\":0.4,\"b\":0.9}, {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0.15,\"m\":0.7,\"y\":0.35,\"k\":0.05}, or {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5}); if your RGB source values are 0-255 bytes, prefer hex '#RRGGBB'. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {"model":"rgb","r":1,"g":0,"b":0} | {"model":"cmyk","c":0,"m":1,"y":1,"k":0} | {"model":"gray","gray":0.5} | {"model":"swatch","name":"PANTONE 185 C","tint":0.5}.

hidden.description: Visibility: true = hide, false = show. Omit for no change. WARNING: Never unhide unless the user's request explicitly mentions hidden state. Ask the user first if unsure.

locked.description: Lock state: true = lock, false = unlock. Omit for no change. WARNING: Never unlock unless the user's request explicitly mentions locked state. Ask the user first if unsure.

overprintFill.description: Overprint fill: true = overprint, false = no overprint. Primarily meaningful for CMYK/spot-color print workflows. Omit for no change.

overprintStroke.description: Overprint stroke: true = overprint, false = no overprint. Primarily meaningful for CMYK/spot-color print workflows. Omit for no change.

strokeCap.description: Line cap style. Omit to leave unchanged.

strokeColor.description: Stroke color. Hex '#RRGGBB', a named document swatch via {\"model\":\"swatch\",\"name\":\"PANTONE 485 C\"}, or a color object (for example {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0.15,\"m\":0.7,\"y\":0.35,\"k\":0.05}). Use 'none' to remove stroke. Omit for no change. For object models rgb/cmyk/gray, prefer normalized channels in [0,1] (for example {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":0.25,\"g\":0.4,\"b\":0.9}, {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0.15,\"m\":0.7,\"y\":0.35,\"k\":0.05}, or {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5}); if your RGB source values are 0-255 bytes, prefer hex '#RRGGBB'. ONLY pass a color when the user explicitly names one; otherwise omit so the tool uses the Color panel's current stroke swatch — do NOT default to black. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {"model":"rgb","r":1,"g":0,"b":0} | {"model":"cmyk","c":0,"m":1,"y":1,"k":0} | {"model":"gray","gray":0.5} | {"model":"swatch","name":"PANTONE 185 C","tint":0.5}.

strokeDash.description: Dash pattern as array of numbers (e.g. [12,4,2,4]). Omit for no change. [] = solid line.

strokeJoin.description: Line join style. Omit to leave unchanged.

strokeWeight.description: Absolute stroke width in points. Omit for no change. Use strokeWeightDelta for relative changes ('increase'/'decrease') — never guess the current value.

strokeWeightDelta.description: Relative stroke width change in points (positive=thicker, negative=thinner). Reads the live current weight and adds this delta, clamped to [0,1000]. Use instead of strokeWeight when the user says 'increase', 'decrease', 'thicker', 'thinner'.

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to style. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: SetAppearance

tools.description: Get details of all artboards including name, locked state, bounds, and valid canvas bounds. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down. Returns artboards[] (the list to iterate) and canvas_bounds ([left,top,right,bottom]).
tools.name: ListArtboards

tools.description: Add a new artboard to the current document. This is the default way to get a new canvas at a different size (book cover, poster, social variant, print format) — an Illustrator document can hold many artboards at different sizes, so new-size requests rarely need CreateDocument. left/top omitted → auto-positions right of the last artboard with a 20pt gap, wrapping to a new row if needed. Coordinates canvas-global, points, Y-down. Must stay within the canvas — see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds. Requires a document open.

artboardName.description: Name for the artboard (auto-generated if empty)

backgroundColor.description: Artboard background color. Use 'none' to leave the artboard transparent. Omit to inherit the document/preference default. Only rgb, cmyk, or 'none' are accepted by AIArtboardSuite — gray and named swatches are rejected. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {"model":"rgb","r":1,"g":0,"b":0} | {"model":"cmyk","c":0,"m":1,"y":1,"k":0} | {"model":"gray","gray":0.5}.

left.description: Left (X) in points. Must be within canvas_bounds returned by ListArtboards. Omit to auto-position to the right of the last artboard.

top.description: Top (Y) in points. Must be within canvas_bounds returned by ListArtboards. Omit to auto-position.

tools.name: CreateArtboard

tools.description: Sets one or more properties of an artboard atomically in a single update. Resolves the target artboard by artboardIndex, then artboardName, then falls back to the active artboard. newName: rename the artboard. backgroundColor: hex ('#RRGGBB' / '#RGB') or structured color objects (rgb / cmyk); 'none' clears the background. Named swatches are not supported. presetName: resize to a named preset (e.g. 'A4', 'iPhone X', 'Instagram Story', 'HDV/HDTV 720'). Always use this for ANY request that names a device, paper size, social-media format, or video standard — even if you know the canonical pixel/point dimensions. Never guess a presetName — call GetArtboardProperties with no arguments first to see every valid name, then pass an exact match. When presetName is used, orientation is auto-detected from the artboard's current width/height so the existing orientation is always preserved by default. Only pass orientation when the user explicitly asks to change it. At least one property must be provided. Prefer this tool over sequential single-property calls when changing multiple properties at once. Resulting artboard bounds must stay within the canvas — see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds.

artboardIndex.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

artboardName.description: Name of the artboard to update (empty to use index or active)

backgroundColor.description: Background color. Use 'none' to clear the background color. Omit to leave unchanged. Only rgb, cmyk, or 'none' are accepted by AIArtboardSuite — gray and named swatches are rejected. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {"model":"rgb","r":1,"g":0,"b":0} | {"model":"cmyk","c":0,"m":1,"y":1,"k":0} | {"model":"gray","gray":0.5}.

newName.description: New name for the artboard (omit to leave unchanged)

orientation.description: Desired orientation for the preset. 'landscape': longer preset dim becomes width. 'portrait': longer preset dim becomes height. 'square': applies the preset's raw dim1/dim2 values as-is without any reordering (only meaningful for genuinely square presets). Omit to auto-detect from the artboard's current width/height (square artboards default to portrait). Only provide when the user explicitly asks to change orientation.

presetName.description: Named preset to apply (e.g. 'A4', 'Instagram Story', 'HDV/HDTV 720'). Case-insensitive. Dimensions are applied according to orientation (auto-detected from current artboard when omitted). Omit to leave dimensions unchanged.

tools.name: SetArtboardProperties

tools.description: Duplicate an existing artboard to newLeft/newTop with an optional new name (auto-generated if empty). Coordinates are canvas-global points, Y-down. When duplicateContent is true the artwork moves with the artboard by the same offset; if the requested position would make the copy overlap the source, it is automatically placed at a non-overlapping position clear of the source and the final coordinates are reported in the response — unless no room remains within the canvas, in which case the call fails with an actionable error. Must stay within the canvas — see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds.

artboardIndex.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

artboardName.description: Name of the artboard to duplicate (empty to use index or active)

duplicateContent.description: Also duplicate artwork on the artboard (default: true)

newLeft.description: Left (X) of the new artboard in points. Must be within canvas_bounds returned by ListArtboards.

newName.description: Name for the duplicated artboard (auto-generated if empty)

newTop.description: Top (Y) of the new artboard in points. Must be within canvas_bounds returned by ListArtboards.

tools.name: DuplicateArtboard

tools.description: Get details of the currently active artboard. Result: artboards[0] contains index, name, locked, bounds [left,top,right,bottom] in Y-down points. Derive width = right - left, height = bottom - top for proportional positioning (e.g. center x = left + width * 0.5, lower-third y = top + height * 0.65).
tools.name: GetActiveArtboard

tools.description: Scale or resize artboards. Do NOT use this tool for named preset requests like 'iPhone X', 'A4', 'Instagram Story', 'HDV/HDTV 720' — use SetArtboardProperties with presetName instead. The 'mode' parameter controls how scaleXValues/scaleYValues are interpreted:   mode='factor': values are multipliers (1.0=no change, 2.0=double, 0.5=halve).   mode='absolute': values are target width/height in points (e.g. 500 means 500pt). Prefer mode='absolute' when the user gives exact dimensions (e.g. '500 by 700 points'). Scaling is applied around per-artboard anchor points (defaults to 'center'). Valid anchors (hyphenated): 'top-left','top-center','top-right','center-left','center','center-right','bottom-left','bottom-center','bottom-right'. Use anchors to pin a specific corner or edge during resize, e.g. anchors=['bottom-right'] keeps the bottom-right corner fixed while the artboard grows/shrinks from the top-left. Artwork scales with the artboard by default (scaleContent=true); set scaleContent=false to resize the artboard only. When scaleContent=true, artwork preserves its own aspect ratio by default (maintainAspectRatioOfContent) even when the artboard itself is resized non-uniformly - see maintainAspectRatioOfContent. All provided arrays must match the length of artboardIndices. Locked artboards are skipped unless force=true. Must stay within the canvas — see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds.

anchors.description: Per-artboard anchor point for scaling origin. Each element must be one of: 'top-left','top-center','top-right','center-left','center','center-right','bottom-left','bottom-center','bottom-right'. Defaults to 'center' for all artboards when omitted.

artboardIndices.description: 1-based artboard indices to scale (1 = first artboard).

force.description: Set true only when user explicitly asks to scale locked artboards.

maintainAspectRatioOfContent.description: Default true. Only affects how artwork is scaled when scaleContent=true - the artboard itself always resizes exactly to scaleXValues[i]/scaleYValues[i], independently per axis, regardless of this setting. When true, artwork is always scaled uniformly to fit within the new artboard size without exceeding either dimension (preserving proportions), and is normally also centered in the new artboard on any axis with leftover space - centering is skipped (aspect ratio is still preserved) only in the rare case content bounds cannot be read. Set to false ONLY when the user explicitly says stretching/squashing/distorting the artwork is acceptable (e.g. 'it's fine if the content stretches', 'squeeze it to fit exactly', 'don't worry about distortion') - this stretches/squashes artwork to exactly match the new artboard dimensions, same as the artboard itself. Otherwise keep the default true.

mode.description: Required. 'factor': scaleXValues/scaleYValues are multipliers. 'absolute': they are target dimensions in points.

scaleContent.description: Scale artwork inside each artboard along with it. Set false to resize artboard only without scaling artwork.

scaleXValues.description: mode='factor': horizontal multiplier per artboard. mode='absolute': target width in points per artboard.

scaleYValues.description: mode='factor': vertical multiplier per artboard. mode='absolute': target height in points per artboard.

tools.name: ScaleArtboards

tools.description: Resize an artboard's bounds to tightly enclose artwork — does NOT change the viewport or zoom level. The 'scope' parameter controls which artwork is considered: 'artboard' (default) fits to any artwork whose bounds intersect the target artboard, even partially; 'all' fits to all artwork in the document; 'selected' fits to currently selected objects; 'objects' fits to specific objects by UUID (requires uuids parameter). Prefer 'objects' when you have UUIDs; use 'selected' only when the user explicitly refers to their current selection. Reports new bounds in details. Note: this tool resizes the artboard itself, not the view. There is no MCP tool for zoom/pan — those are view-only actions handled by the app's View menu. Locked artboards are protected by default and cannot be fit unless force=true. Resulting artboard bounds must stay within the canvas — see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds.

artboardIndex.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

artboardName.description: Name of the artboard (empty to use index or active)

force.description: Default false. Set to true only when the user explicitly asks to fit a locked artboard. General requests like 'fit all artboards except locked ones' must leave this false.

scope.description: Which artwork to fit: 'artboard' (overlapping target artboard, default), 'all' (all artwork in document), 'selected' (currently selected objects — fails if nothing is selected), 'objects' (specific UUIDs — must also provide uuids parameter).

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to fit to. Required when scope='objects'. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: FitArtboard

tools.description: Remove an artboard from the document. By default the artwork on the artboard is preserved; set removeContent=true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete the artwork too. Returns the updated artboard list with new indices after deletion. This tool deletes artboards only, not layers. artboardName must be an artboard name from ListArtboards. removeContent only controls whether artwork on the deleted artboard is also removed; it does not delete layers by name. Locked artboards are protected by default and cannot be deleted unless force=true. Set force=true only when the user explicitly asks to delete a locked artboard. To delete individual objects or layers without removing the artboard, use DeleteObjects instead. Cannot remove the last artboard — a document must have at least one artboard. If only one artboard exists and you need different dimensions, position, or name, use ScaleArtboards, MoveArtboards, or SetArtboardProperties instead.

artboardIndex.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

artboardName.description: Artboard name from ListArtboards (not a layer name; empty to use index or active)

force.description: Default false. Set to true only when the user explicitly asks to delete a locked artboard. General requests like 'delete all artboards except locked ones' must leave this false.

removeContent.description: Default false. Set to true only when the user explicitly asks to also delete the artwork on the artboard (e.g. 'delete the artboard and its contents'). Generic requests like 'delete the artboard' or 'remove artboard 2' must leave this false — the artboard is removed but its artwork is preserved.

tools.name: DeleteArtboard

tools.description: Set a specific artboard as active and selected. Locked or hidden artboards become active but may not be selected.

artboardIndex.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

artboardName.description: Name of the artboard to set as active (empty to use index)

tools.name: SetActiveArtboard

tools.description: Reposition multiple artboards in a single batch operation. Artwork on each artboard moves with it by default (moveContent=true). This tool snapshots art-to-artboard associations before any moves, so artboards can safely swap positions or overlap during rearrangement without stealing each other's content, as long as every affected artboard's move is included in this same call — never split one interdependent rearrangement across multiple calls. All three arrays must have the same length. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down. Must stay within the canvas — see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds. Locked artboards are skipped unless force=true. NOTE: Artboard frames are committed before art transforms; transforming art may partially fail, so the result may include successfully moved artboards with partially transformed content.

artboardIndices.description: 1-based artboard indices to move (1 = first artboard). Must match lengths of newLefts and newTops.

force.description: Default false. Set true only when user explicitly asks to move locked artboards. General requests like 'rearrange all unlocked artboards' must leave this false.

moveContent.description: Move artwork inside each artboard along with it (default: true).

newLefts.description: New left (X) position for each artboard in points.

newTops.description: New top (Y) position for each artboard in points (Y-down).

tools.name: MoveArtboards

tools.description: Look up artboard presets available in Illustrator (Print, Web, Video, Social, Branding, Mobile). Each preset reports dim1_pt and dim2_pt — the raw values returned by the Illustrator preset table. Mobile preset dimensions are screen pixels (= points at Illustrator's 72-PPI screen baseline, matching the Artboard Properties panel). Pass presetName for an exact (case-insensitive) lookup of a single preset; omit to list all presets. Never guess a presetName — call with no arguments first to see every valid name, then pass an exact match. Pass category to filter by category when listing all.

category.description: Category filter when listing all presets. One of: 'Print', 'Web', 'Video', 'Social', 'Branding', 'Mobile'. Ignored when presetName is provided.

presetName.description: Preset name for an exact case-insensitive lookup (e.g. 'A4', 'Instagram Story').

tools.name: GetArtboardProperties

tools.description: Browse the document's layer hierarchy. Returns objects_basic_details array with basic details per node: uuid, name, object_type, bounds (when present), child_count, child_types, locked (when true), hidden (when true) — both inherited from ancestors; is_generative (when true), generative_type (when present), has_edit_lineage (when true); and current_layer (when available) with the uuid and locked/hidden state of the document's active layer. Layers and children are in z-order (0=frontmost/top). Use this to explore layers and groups top-down. To get all objects on a specific artboard instead, use GetArtboardStructure. Use 'maxDepth' to control depth: -1 = unlimited (all descendants), 0 (default) = top-level only, 1 = immediate children, 2+ = deeper. Nodes at the depth limit show child_count/child_types summary instead of children. Omit 'uuids' to start from document layers. Pass 'uuids' to start from specific objects (groups, layers, etc.). For detailed properties (text_content, geometry), use GetObjectStructure. LARGE RESPONSES: Children are expanded breadth-first (all siblings at each depth before going deeper). When the response size limit is reached, expansion stops — groups already listed retain child_count/child_types summaries for navigation. Results include truncated=true and resume_hint. Call GetObjectStructure on specific group UUIDs to drill deeper.

maxDepth.description: Depth of children to include. 0 = starting nodes only (default). 1 = starting nodes + immediate children. 2+ = deeper. -1 = unlimited (all descendants). Groups/layers at the depth limit show child_count and child_types summary instead of children.

uuids.description: Optional array of object UUIDs to use as starting points. Omit to start from document layers (default). Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetCanvasStructure

tools.description: Get all objects visually overlapping an artboard, regardless of which layer they belong to. Returns artboards (index, bounds) and objects_basic_details array in z-order (0=frontmost/top). To browse by layer hierarchy instead, use GetCanvasStructure. Each object includes uuid, name, object_type, bounds, is_selected, locked (when true), hidden (when true) — both inherited from ancestors; is_generative (when true), generative_type (when present), has_edit_lineage (when true); groups also have child_count and child_types. Groups are NOT recursively expanded — call GetObjectStructure on a group uuid to inspect contents. LARGE RESPONSES: When too many objects exist, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

artboardIndex.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use the active artboard.

tools.name: GetArtboardStructure

tools.description: Get the selection roots (the objects the user actually selected, not descendants of an already-selected parent), in z-order (0=frontmost/top). Returns objects_basic_details array; each entry has uuid, name, object_type, bounds, locked (when true), hidden (when true) — both inherited from ancestors; is_generative (when true), generative_type (when present), has_edit_lineage (when true); groups also have child_count and child_types. To inspect a selected group's contents, call GetObjectStructure on its uuid. LARGE RESPONSES: When too many objects are selected, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.
tools.name: VisualizeSelection

tools.description: Create a new, separate Illustrator file. Most tasks do NOT need one — an Illustrator document holds many artboards at different sizes, and keeping variants (book cover, poster, social sizes, print formats) in one file lets the user compare and export them together. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a new file, or the required colorMode/units/bleed differs from the current document. For a new canvas at a different size in the current document, use CreateArtboard. Returns the initial artboard's bounds and index in artboards.

artboardBackgroundColor.description: Initial artboard background color. Use 'none' for no background. Omit to use the application default. Only rgb, cmyk, or 'none' are accepted by AIArtboardSuite — named swatches are rejected. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {"model":"rgb","r":1,"g":0,"b":0} | {"model":"cmyk","c":0,"m":1,"y":1,"k":0} | {"model":"gray","gray":0.5}.

bleed.description: Document bleed in the specified units. Pass [value] for uniform bleed on all sides, or 4 per-side values [left, top, right, bottom]. Exactly 1 or 4 values accepted. All values must be >= 0.

height.description: Artboard height in the specified units (default: points)

rasterEffectsResolution.description: Raster effects resolution (affects live effects like drop shadows)

units.description: Document ruler units. Use short form 'mm' (not 'millimeters')

width.description: Artboard width in the specified units (default: points)

tools.name: CreateDocument

tools.description: Opens an existing file in Illustrator. Returns document metadata and artboard details so you can immediately start working. The previously active document remains open and can be switched back to with SwitchDocument.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file to open (supports ~ for home directory). Must be provided by the user — never guess or fabricate file paths.

tools.name: OpenDocument

tools.description: Lists all open documents with metadata. The active document includes full details: colorMode, units, artboardCount, bleedInsets, rasterEffectsResolution, colorProfiles, width, height, document_profile (Print/Web/Video/Mobile), document_title (string, from XMP dc:title), and document_language (string, e.g. 'en-US', from XMP dc:language). Inactive documents include name, path, and index.
tools.name: ListDocuments

tools.description: Switches the active document by index, name, or file path. Returns full document metadata and artboard details for the newly active document. Use ListDocuments first to see available documents. Provide exactly one of: index, name, or filePath.

filePath.description: Document file path to switch to

index.description: Document index from ListDocuments (0-based). Omit to use name or filePath instead.

tools.name: SwitchDocument

tools.description: Exports artwork to a file, returns it as a stream, or uploads it to an Adobe-hosted URL. Supports raster formats (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PSD, WEBP, BMP), vector formats (SVG, PDF, EPS, DWG, DXF), and native Illustrator format (AI). Target what to export: CANVAS (entire document, default), ARTBOARD (single artboard by index), UUID (specific objects by uuid — no selection needed), or SELECTION (currently selected objects). Output goes to one of three places: provide `outputPath` for file mode (default), `outputMode='stream'` for inline data (PNG/SVG only), or `uploadTo` for a direct upload to a presigned URL. For the presigned-upload flow: obtain uploadTo from the host's canvas-upload preparation step and pass it here exactly as given; leave authBearer unset — a presigned URL already carries its own signature, and adding a Bearer header breaks it. No `url` is returned in `details` for this path (it's a raw-byte PUT, not a harness POST); success just means the bytes are uploaded, and the caller resolves the final asset URL in a separate step. Never guess a value for uploadTo/authBearer yourself. For file mode, provide outputPath with a full path. Host OS comes only from client_platform on each prompt (macos|windows) — never infer OS from user path syntax. Passing a group or layer UUID exports all children within that container. Omit optional styling parameters (antiAlias, backgroundColor, quality, colorModel, etc.) unless the user explicitly asked for them — when omitted, the user's saved Export Preferences are used. Never guess their values. Do not use this tool for a Save or Save As request — exporting is not saving.

aiIncludeLinkedFiles.description: AI: When true, embeds linked images and placed EPS files into the saved AI file. When false, no additional embedding occurs — files that are currently linked remain linked, but already-embedded content is not affected.

antiAlias.description: Anti-aliasing. Applies to: PNG, JPEG, PSD, WebP, TIFF, BMP.

artboardIndex.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use the active artboard.

authBearer.description: Leave unset for the presigned-upload flow (uploadTo from the host's canvas-upload preparation step) — a presigned URL already carries its own signature, and adding a Bearer header breaks it. Only set this for the separate multipart-POST harness-upload contract.

backgroundColor.description: Background color for export. Applies to: WEBP ('transparent' or any '#RRGGBB'), PNG ('transparent' or any '#RRGGBB').

collisionStrategy.description: How to handle an existing file at outputPath. When no leaf filename is given (path ends in a separator or resolves to an existing directory), 'error' is changed to 'autoSuffix' — UNLESS you explicitly pass 'overwrite', which is still honored for a derived leaf. 'error' (default) fails the call and surfaces the conflict to the user — ALWAYS use this when you supplied an explicit leaf filename; do NOT silently rename or replace it. 'overwrite' replaces the existing file — permitted ONLY when the user's current message explicitly instructs you to overwrite or replace it (e.g. 'overwrite it', 'replace the file'). Re-issuing the same export request, even to the same path, expresses export intent, not overwrite permission; nor does a prior overwrite approval or a path you chose earlier in this task. 'autoSuffix' appends '-2', '-3', ... until unique — this is also the default fallback for a derived leaf when 'overwrite' was not requested; with an explicit leaf filename, set it yourself ONLY to stay collision-safe when iterating over multiple objects. When in doubt with an explicit filename, use 'error' and ask the user.

colorModel.description: Color model. Applies to: JPEG (RGB/CMYK/grayscale), PSD (RGB/CMYK/grayscale), TIFF (RGB/CMYK/grayscale), BMP (RGB/grayscale/bitmap).

embedColorProfile.description: Embed ICC color profile. Applies to: JPEG, WEBP, AI, PSD, TIFF. Not applicable to PDF.

format.description: Export format. 'AI' is Adobe Illustrator native format (.ai). JPG is an alias for JPEG; TIF is an alias for TIFF. EPS hard-fails with an error if the document contains broken linked files; all other formats in file mode include a non-fatal warning in the response `warnings` array.

outputMode.description: 'file' saves to the specified outputPath; 'stream' returns inline data (PNG/SVG only). Ignored when uploadTo is set.

outputPath.description: Output file path. Required for file mode. Use client_platform on the prompt (macos|windows) for host OS when composing default paths — never infer OS from user path shape. User-given paths → verbatim; never silently remap (e.g. do not rewrite C:\\... to ~/...). If an explicit user path conflicts with client_platform, explain the mismatch and ask for a path valid on this host. `~` = user profile; use client_platform for separators when composing paths. Never use %VAR% tokens. Mac (client_platform=macos): ~, /Volumes/..., /Users/Shared, /tmp, /var/folders/..., ~/Library/CloudStorage, ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs; blocked: other ~/Library sub-paths, other users, OS dirs. Win (client_platform=windows): ~, D:\\, E:\\..., ~\\AppData\\Local\\Temp; blocked: ~\\AppData\\Roaming, ~\\AppData\\Local (except Temp), Program Files, ProgramData, C:\\Users\\Public, app folder, other users, OS dirs, UNC. Verify root before calling. No filename from the user? Omit the leaf — pass a folder path ending with / (e.g. ~/Desktop/<<DOC_NAME>>/); the tool fills the filename from the target's own name. Don't look the name up yourself. Mutually exclusive with uploadTo.

pdfPreset.description: PDF: Pick a custom (user-created) preset by its exact catalog name; for built-in presets use pdfPresetRole. An unknown name fails with the list of installed presets. If neither is set, export reuses the last-used PDF settings (the document's own saved PDF settings, else the app's last export preference).

pdfPresetRole.description: PDF: Pick a built-in Adobe PDF preset by its locale-independent role. Use this for any built-in preset — display names are localized (e.g. 'High Quality Print' shows a different name on non-English installs), so a role is the only reliable selector. Wins over pdfPreset if both are set.

resolution.description: DPI for raster exports (PNG, JPEG, PSD, WEBP, TIFF, BMP). Screen baseline is 72 DPI — use this to convert scale factors: 0.5x=36, 0.75x=54, 1x=72, 2x=144, 3x=216. Always pass this when the prompt specifies a scale factor or resolution.

svgFont.description: SVG: How fonts are handled. 'svg' embeds font data as SVG font definitions in the output (SVG), 'outline' converts text to vector outlines eliminating font dependencies (Convert To Outlines).

svgImages.description: SVG: How raster images are handled. 'embed' encodes images as base64 data URIs, 'link' writes sidecar image files next to the SVG, 'preserve' keeps the original link/embed state from the source document. In outputMode='stream' all modes are normalized to 'embed' so the returned SVG is self-contained.

svgStyling.description: SVG: How style properties are written. 'inline' puts them in element style attributes (Inline Style), 'css' emits a <style> block with class selectors (Internal CSS), 'presentationAttributes' uses presentation attributes on elements.

uploadTo.description: Presigned upload URL obtained from the host's canvas-upload preparation step — pass it exactly as given, never construct or guess one yourself. Only Adobe-owned hosts are accepted (*.adobe.io / *.adobe.com, or known Adobe S3 backends for the presigned flow). Mutually exclusive with outputPath. Leave authBearer unset for this flow (empty authBearer = raw-bytes PUT to a presigned URL, no `url` in the response). Non-empty authBearer instead selects the separate multipart-POST harness-upload contract (response's `url` returned in `details`) — do not mix the two.

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects, groups, or layers to export. Pass one or more UUIDs when targetType=UUID. Get UUIDs from GetCanvasStructure. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: Export

tools.description: Captures artwork as a PNG file for visual inspection. Returns a preview_path field with the file location — read that file to view the image. For permanent file exports (PNG/JPEG/SVG/PDF), use Export instead. Use this to verify your work AFTER completing a batch of related changes. Avoid calling more than 2-3 times per task unless debugging a specific visual issue. width/height control max output dimensions in pixels (max 1024 each, total pixel area capped at 512x512). To inspect a specific region at higher detail, use cropX/cropY/cropWidth/cropHeight to specify a bounding box in points. Default target is CANVAS.

artboardIndex.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use the active artboard.

cropHeight.description: Crop region height in points. 0 = no crop (use full target bounds).

cropWidth.description: Crop region width in points. 0 = no crop (use full target bounds).

cropX.description: Crop region left edge in points (canvas-global, Y-down). When cropWidth and cropHeight are both > 0, only this rectangular area is captured. Use GetActiveArtboard to find artboard bounds.

cropY.description: Crop region top edge in points (canvas-global, Y-down).

height.description: Max height of the exported image in pixels (default: 400, maximum: 1024). Total pixel area is capped at 512*512.

reason.description: Brief reason for this visual check (e.g., 'verify layout after placing all stat cards')

targetType.description: One of: CANVAS, SELECTION, ARTBOARD, or UUID. Default: CANVAS (entire document).

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects, groups, or layers to capture. Pass one or more UUIDs when targetType=UUID. Get UUIDs from GetCanvasStructure. Always pass an array, even for one object.

width.description: Max width of the exported image in pixels (default: 400, maximum: 1024). Total pixel area is capped at 512*512.

tools.name: CapturePreview

tools.description: Batch query and update tool for object properties (color, weight, font, text content). Prefer over structural browsing when you need bulk data (e.g. every object's color for grouping or auditing) — omit matchCriteria, pass returnFields:['color'] to get all fill/stroke values in one call without walking the hierarchy. Also finds objects by exact criteria (not fuzzy/visual categories — 'lines' aren't a distinct type from other paths, see 'objectTypes') and optionally writes setProperties (fillColor/strokeColor/strokeWeight) onto every match in the same call. Use this match-and-set path when the targets must be discovered here — by criteria (e.g. 'change all red shapes to blue') or every object (e.g. 'make the whole illustration blue'); when you already hold the UUIDs or need nuanced color (e.g. luminance-aware grayscale), use SetAppearance instead. setProperties can never write text content (use ReplaceText) or font (use ReplaceFont). Omit 'setProperties' to run in query mode: matches are reported (shape controlled by 'returnFields') and nothing is written. Provide 'setProperties' to write onto every match instead — its keys don't need to match matchCriteria's 1:1 (e.g. match fillColor, set strokeWeight). Omit 'matchCriteria' to target every object matching 'objectTypes' unconditionally, in either mode. Write mode: locked/hidden objects are matched but never written to (reported in failed_objects). Query mode: the walk may stop at the response size limit — success_count reflects matches found so far, not necessarily every match in the document.

matchCriteria.description: Criteria to match, e.g. {\"fillColor\":\"#FF0000\"}, {\"strokeWeight\":2}, {\"fontFamily\":\"Myriad Pro\"}, {\"searchText\":\"Lorem ipsum\"}. Keys: fillColor/strokeColor (hex '#RRGGBB', swatch {\"model\":\"swatch\",\"name\":\"PANTONE 485 C\"}, color {model:'cmyk'|'rgb'|'gray',...}, or 'none'), strokeWeight (number), fontFamily/fontStyle (strings, checked against document usage not installed fonts; require objectTypes 'text' or omitted), searchText (string, same search as ReplaceText — multiple occurrences in one frame still count as one match; require objectTypes 'text' or omitted), caseSensitive/wholeWord (booleans, default true, require searchText). Omit (or pass {}) to match every object visited by 'objectTypes' unconditionally.

objectTypes.description: Omit to visit every object in the document — the default when targeting all objects. Provide objectTypes only when the request explicitly names a specific category: 'path' (paths, compound paths), 'mesh' (gradient meshes — fill-only, no stroke), 'text' (text frames). Always pass an array, even for one type.

returnFields.description: Query mode only; rejected with 'setProperties'. Fields per matched object: 'uuid', 'bounds' (GetBounds convention), 'color' ({fill,stroke} — each a color object or null if unpainted; mesh stroke is always null; mixed objects add fillIsMixed/strokeIsMixed:true when values disagree), 'textRanges' (character offsets of matched runs/occurrences within text frames — requires matchCriteria fontFamily or searchText; shape: [{start,end},...]; request when a follow-up tool needs sub-frame positions, omit for frame-level queries). Omit 'returnFields' for uuid only — each extra field costs an additional lookup per match.

setProperties.description: Values to set on every match. Omit to run in query mode instead. Supports only fillColor/strokeColor/strokeWeight (same formats as 'matchCriteria'). Keys don't need to match matchCriteria's 1:1. At least one key required when provided.

startAfterUuid.description: Resume cursor for a truncated query-mode match list: pass the previous response's resume_after_uuid to continue after that point (only reliable if the document/params are unchanged). Rejected with an error if the uuid isn't found among current matches (e.g. the document changed) — omit startAfterUuid and retry to start over from the first match instead of guessing. Query mode only.

tools.name: FindObjects

tools.description: Traces a raster or placed image into vectors with Image Trace, or expands an existing live Image Trace into a final vector group. To preserve the user's original, always DUPLICATE the source image first (e.g. with DuplicateObjects) and run this tool on the duplicate's `uuid` — never trace the original directly. Offset the duplicate so it sits BESIDE the original with a small gap — not overlapping it (e.g. DuplicateObjects offsetX/offsetY), keeping it within the canvas bounds where possible. (This applies only when `uuid` is a source raster/placed image; when it is already a live tracing you are re-tracing or expanding, operate on it directly — do not duplicate.) Before tracing, determine what the image actually is — its content is NOT in the object metadata, so do not guess from it. Unless you have already seen the image this turn, inspect the actual pixels first — the selected image, or the whole canvas when nothing is selected — using whatever image-inspection capability you have, then pass the `preset` that matches what you saw. If no preset matches the requested look or exact settings, pick the CLOSEST one, run it as `trace_live` (re-runnable, so the user can review), and say clearly in your reply which preset you used and that it's the closest approximation, not exact. `action` controls the result: by default it stays a LIVE, editable Image Trace (`trace_live`); it is expanded into a final vector group only when the user asks. On success, `trace_and_expand` always consumes the input `uuid` — use the returned `uuid`. `expand` consumes the input only if it's an existing live Image Trace; otherwise it's a no-op and the input `uuid` remains valid — see `details`. `trace_live` never consumes the input — the source is retained (embedded in the tracing), and the returned `uuid` is the (possibly new) tracing object. If a call fails, re-fetch current document state rather than retrying the input `uuid`.

action.description:
What to do with the object at `uuid`:
- trace_live (default): trace into a live, editable Image Trace and LEAVE IT LIVE — nothing finalized. The trace stays live so the user can review and tune it. If `uuid` is already a live tracing, re-applies the preset.
- trace_and_expand: trace, then immediately expand into a final, editable vector group. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to finalize / expand / flatten the trace. If `uuid` is already a live tracing, re-applies the preset then expands. This REPLACES the traced object in place — the resulting group becomes the artwork and that object no longer exists; because you trace a duplicate (see above), the user's original image is preserved.
- expand: expand an existing live Image Trace into a final vector group; pass preset 'none'. Use when the user asks to finalize an existing live tracing. If `uuid` isn't a live tracing (e.g. already expanded), report that there's nothing to expand — don't expand a different object.
To retry with a different preset, do NOT delete the result — deleting it does not restore the original image; use Undo instead. trace_live (the default) is re-runnable when the preset is uncertain.

preset.description:
The Image Trace preset to apply. For the expand action pass 'none'. For trace_live or trace_and_expand, pick the single preset that best matches the image you inspected — what it is (photo, logo, icon, line drawing, sketch), how many colors it has, and color vs. grayscale — not guessed from metadata:
- none: no preset; expand action only.
- autoColor: full-color trace where Illustrator decides the number of colors. Use only for genuinely full-color or complex images whose colors matter and no more specific preset fits; do not fall back to it when the image content is unclear — determine the content first.
- highColor: full color, high number of colors. For detailed, vivid color art.
- lowColor: full color reduced to ~16 colors. For simpler color art or a flatter look.
- threeColors: exactly 3 colors. For bold, minimal color graphics.
- sixColors: exactly 6 colors. For flat graphics with a small palette.
- sixteenColors: exactly 16 colors. For flat graphics, moderate palette.
- highFidelityPhoto: full-color photo trace preserving the most detail. For realistic photographs.
- lowFidelityPhoto: full-color photo trace with fewer colors. Simpler, posterized photo look.
- grayscale: shades of gray. For black-and-white photographs or gray images.
- shadesOfGray: grayscale with fewer tones, for a flatter monochrome result.
- blackAndWhite: two-tone black and white. For high-contrast images, stamps, or simple marks.
- outline: edges as black strokes on transparent bg. For line drawings you want as strokes, not fills.
- lineArt: clean black-and-white line work. For crisp inked drawings or comic art.
- sketchedArt: black-and-white trace tuned for hand-drawn sketches and pencil work.
- technicalDrawing: black-and-white trace for precise, fine-detail line drawings, e.g. blueprints/schematics.
- silhouettes: solid black shapes. Bold filled silhouettes.
- blackAndWhiteLogo: black-and-white trace tuned for simple logos and marks.

uuid.description: UUID of the object to operate on (from the canvas/object summary): a raster or placed image to trace, or an existing live Image Trace to expand or re-trace with a different preset. When tracing, this should be a duplicate you created (see the tool description), not the user's original.

tools.name: Vectorize

tools.description: Creates a new layer with the specified name. Position defaults to front (top) of the layer stack. Use parentID to create a sublayer inside an existing layer. For 'above:<uuid>' or 'below:<uuid>', the new layer is created as a sibling of the reference layer (same nesting level). Layers cannot be placed inside groups — only into other layers. Returns the new layer identifier in the top-level `uuid` field.

parentID.description: UUID of a parent layer to create the sublayer inside. When provided, 'front'/'back' place at top/bottom inside that layer. Ignored when position is 'above:<uuid>' or 'below:<uuid>'. Omit to create at the top level.

position.description: Where to place in the z-order: 'front' (topmost, default), 'back' (bottommost), 'above:<uuid>' (above referenced object), 'below:<uuid>' (below referenced object). When parentID is provided, 'front'/'back' place inside that container. 'above:<uuid>'/'below:<uuid>' always place relative to the referenced object — parentID is ignored. When replacing an object (including placing a Firefly-edited version back), use 'above:<uuid-of-original>' to preserve its stacking position — and always call this tool BEFORE deleting the original; deleting first causes PlaceImage to fail with 'Reference object not found'.

tools.name: CreateLayer

tools.description: Get detailed visual appearance properties for one or more objects. Response format: {success, details, visual_appearance: [{uuid, properties: {fill_stack, stroke_stack, has_fill, has_stroke, opacity, blend_mode, graphic_style, mask_context, is_clip_path, hidden, locked}}, ...]}. Each result includes: fill_stack (array), stroke_stack (array), has_fill (boolean), has_stroke (boolean), opacity (number), blend_mode (string), graphic_style (string|null), mask_context (object with is_clipping_mask and clipped_by), is_clip_path (boolean — true when this path is the clipping mask path inside a clipping group), hidden (boolean), locked (boolean). For gradient fills/strokes, the color entry includes: model='gradient', gradientType, angle, length, origin, and a stops array where each stop has rampPoint (0-100), midPoint, opacity, and a color object. To change only angle or gradientType on an existing gradient, use SetGradient PATCH mode (omit colors+positions entirely — no need to read stops first). To replace stops while keeping the same count/positions as a reference, read the stops here then rebuild colors[] from each stop's color field and positions[] from each stop's rampPoint, and pass them to SetGradient CREATE mode. Use this when you need to analyze visual styling. To confirm a color/appearance-named target, call this with the candidate UUIDs. BATCH PROCESSING: When analyzing multiple objects, pass array of UUIDs to get all results in one call. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetVisualAppearance

tools.description: Get detailed geometry properties for one or more path/shape objects. Response format: {success, details, geometry_refinement: [{uuid, properties: {transformation_matrix?, is_proportionally_scaled?, path_topology}}, ...]}. Fields vary by art type: transformation_matrix (6-element [a,b,c,d,tx,ty] array) and is_proportionally_scaled (bool — true when scaleX and scaleY differ by less than 2%) are present only for symbol, raster, placed, and text frame art. path_topology for simple paths: {is_closed (bool), segment_count (int)}. path_topology for compound paths: {winding_order (even_odd|non_zero), child_count, path_count, total_segment_count, nested_compound_count}. Use this when you need to analyze geometric construction. BATCH PROCESSING: When analyzing multiple paths, pass array of UUIDs to get all results in one call. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetGeometry

tools.description: Get detailed typography properties for one or more text objects including text content, length, and overflow status. Use this to read text content and character indices. Response format: {success, details, typography_metrics: [{uuid, properties: {...}}, ...]}. Each result properties: text_length (number), text_content? (string), has_text_overflow? (boolean), font_runs (array of font entries — each entry: {font_family (string), font_style? (string), is_font_missing (boolean — true when the font is substituted or unavailable), is_font_embeddable (boolean — true when font permits embedding)}; always present for text frames; empty array for empty frames, 1 entry for single-font frames, multiple entries for mixed-font frames; use this to enumerate ALL fonts in a text frame), font_family? (deprecated, same as font_runs[0].font_family), font_style? (deprecated, same as font_runs[0].font_style), is_font_missing? (deprecated, same as font_runs[0].is_font_missing), is_font_embeddable? (deprecated, same as font_runs[0].is_font_embeddable), font_caps? (string: normal|all_caps|small_caps|all_small_caps — ATE capitalization option for the story; rendered case may differ from text_content, e.g. all_caps with stored lowercase), font_size? (number), tracking? (number), kerning? (string), leading? (number), leading_type? (string), auto_leading? (boolean), baseline_shift? (number), paragraph_alignment? (string), horizontal_scale? (number, percentage 0-100+), vertical_scale? (number, percentage 0-100+). Callers must not assume any ? property is present. BATCH PROCESSING: When analyzing multiple text frames, pass array of UUIDs to get all results in one call. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

uuids.description: UUIDs of text objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetTypographyMetrics

includeTypes.description: Filter: only include objects of these types in children. Groups and layers are always traversed to find matching descendants. Empty = no filter.

maxDepth.description: Maximum recursion depth for groups. -1 = unlimited (default). 0 = root object only, no children expanded. 1 = immediate children only. 2+ = deeper. Groups at maxDepth show child_count and child_types summary.

startAfterUuid.description: Resume cursor for re-expanding a group whose children were previously cut short. This ONE cursor value is checked against EACH requested top-level uuid's OWN direct children, in the order given: whichever uuid's children actually contain it resumes from the NEXT sibling after it, and that consumes the cursor — every OTHER uuid in the same call (whether listed before or after the match) is simply expanded fresh from its own first child instead, which is the expected behavior, not an error. This means you can safely combine one resuming (partial) uuid together with any number of fresh/untouched uuids in a single call. If no uuid in the call contains a match at all, every uuid is expanded fresh from its own first child. Only affects the direct children of the top-level uuids in THIS call, not nested descendants. Empty = start every uuid fresh from the first child as usual.

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetObjectStructure

tools.description: Get bounds for one or more objects. Returns visual bounds that include live effect expansion (e.g. a Gaussian blur with radius=20 expands bounds ~36pt per side). Empty groups/layers have no bounds and are reported in failed_objects. Lightweight alternative to GetGeometry for layout calculations. Supports batch via uuids array. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetBounds

tools.description: Cleans up messy or hand-drawn paths by reducing anchor points and/or smoothing jaggedness. This EDITS geometry — it approximates the original shape within a tolerance, it does not preserve it exactly. Higher curvePrecision / lower smoothingPercentage = closer to the original but less cleanup; lower curvePrecision / higher smoothingPercentage = more aggressive cleanup but more shape drift. mode='simplify': reduces the number of anchor points within a curve-fit tolerance (same as Object > Path > Simplify) — use when a path has too many/dense anchor points. In mode='simplify' (only), pointsAfter is guaranteed never to exceed pointsBefore: at a very high curvePrecision the curve-fit can technically need more anchors than it started with, in which case that path is left as it was rather than made worse. If pointsAfter equals pointsBefore, pass a lower curvePrecision and re-call to actually reduce anchors — omitting curvePrecision uses the application's Simplify preference (often high/conservative) and will not by itself reduce anchors further. mode='smooth': repositions anchor points/handles to remove jaggedness WITHOUT reducing point count (same as the Smooth tool) — use when lines look jagged, rough, or hand-drawn. mode='both' (default): smooths first, then simplifies the result — use for general 'clean up this path' / 'make the lines cleaner' requests. The pointsAfter<=pointsBefore guarantee above only covers the simplify step itself; if smoothing increases anchor count, the final pointsAfter can still exceed the original pointsBefore. curvePrecision/angleThreshold/smoothingPercentage are optional. When curvePrecision is omitted, the application's Simplify preference (GetTolerance) is used. When angleThreshold is omitted, the application's Simplify preference (GetAngleThresold) is used. When smoothingPercentage is omitted, it auto-calibrates per path (same as the Smooth tool's default). Only affects anchors that are curve points; anchors explicitly marked as corner points (e.g. straight polygon-style paths with no curve handles) are intentionally left untouched by design — this matches Illustrator's own Simplify/Smooth, which never round off a rectangle's corners either. If a call reports success but pointsBefore equals pointsAfter with no meaningful bounds change, the path is likely all corner points and not a candidate for cleanup. Only path objects with 3+ anchor points are eligible — groups, compound paths, text, and paths with fewer anchors are skipped, not treated as failures (reported in `results` with skipped=true and a reason). For groups, use GetObjectStructure to expand to path children first, then pass those uuids — compound paths and text cannot be decomposed into individual paths by any tool and are simply not supported. Returns per-object anchor-point counts and bounding boxes before/after — YOU are responsible for checking that delta and re-calling with lower precision/percentage (or telling the user) if the shape drifted more than intended; the tool does not enforce shape fidelity itself.

angleThreshold.description: Simplify corner-preservation angle threshold in degrees (0-180). Used when mode is 'simplify' or 'both'. Omit to use the application default.

curvePrecision.description: Simplify curve-fit precision (0-100, higher = closer fit = more points kept). Used when mode is 'simplify' or 'both'. For genuinely jagged/wobbly hand-drawn input, values above ~20 often produce NO visible reduction — check pointsAfter in the response, and if it didn't drop, retry with a lower value (single digits if needed) rather than assuming it worked. A path with truly chaotic, independent-random anchor placement (not the smoother back-and-forth wobble of a real hand tremor) may still resist a large reduction even at low curvePrecision — that's an inherent curve-fitting limit (more erratic input needs more control points to represent within any tolerance), not a parameter to keep lowering indefinitely. Omit curvePrecision to use the application's Simplify preference instead of guessing.

mode.description: Cleanup mode: 'simplify' reduces anchor point count, 'smooth' removes jaggedness without changing point count, 'both' smooths then simplifies.

smoothingPercentage.description: Smoothing strength (0-100, same scale as the Smooth tool/pathItem.smootheningPercentage). Used when mode is 'smooth' or 'both'. Omit to auto-calibrate per path.

uuids.description: UUIDs of path objects to clean up. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: CleanupPath

tools.description: Single-traversal production QA inspection of the active document. Walks the art tree once and returns a categorized JSON report of findings aggregated by issue tag, each with a display_name, count, and affected_objects[] array; UUIDs and raw fact fields (effective PPI, stroke widths, font license types, etc.) are per affected object, not per aggregated finding. Available scopes: document (color mode, profile, bleed, units, metadata, artboard checks), images (resolution, embedded size, pixel dimensions, color space, missing embedded ICC on linked placed rasters), links (broken, modified, damaged), text (fonts: missing, embeddability, license; text frames: overset, sizing, scaling, leading), colors (fill/stroke colors, spot colors, strokes, overprint white/black/non-black, rich black CMYK detection, raster effects), objects (scale, visibility, position, empty groups, locked state, objects near trim edge / bleed extension). Only the requested scopes are executed and emitted in the response — use this to focus on a specific concern and reduce response size. Omit `scopes` (or pass an empty array) to run all domains. Response shape: top-level `checks` object keyed by category (document/images/links/text/colors/objects), each with a `findings` array (+ optional `partial: true`); top-level `summary` object holds counts and context (total_issues, categories_with_issues, document_context, scopes). `details` is a short human-readable status line (e.g. \"findings=3 categories=2\") meant for logging/display. Read findings from `checks.<category>.findings` and counts from `summary`. Tool returns raw facts only — findings are pre-aggregated by issue tag with `display_name` and `affected_objects[]`. No severity in JSON. PREFLIGHT SEVERITY: Classify per the user's stated output moment (print/export/share/screen). If the user did not state a moment, derive it from the document context in the response: is_print_doc=true → treat as print; is_print_doc=false → treat as screen. If is_print_doc is absent or ambiguous, default to print. Always state which moment you assumed and why. Must fix: the violation is irreversible at output time regardless of designer intent. Needs review: threshold violated but correctness depends on designer intent or context. Always classify as Needs review regardless of output moment: text_size_minimum, stroke_hairline, dash_too_short, overprint_on_non_black, zero_dimension_object, object_too_close_to_trim_edge. What's fine: positive observations (e.g. fonts present, color mode correct) — derive from what the tool did NOT report; never place failed findings here; omit this section entirely when you have no positive observations to make. Scope selection from the user's prompt: targeted request that names ONE attribute → pass matching `scopes` and report ONLY that attribute (do NOT expand into adjacent prepress checks even if returned; surface any extras as a single footnote line). Multi-attribute request (2+ named attributes, e.g. 'check color mode, bleed, spot colors, and hairline strokes') → pass all matching scopes for ALL named attributes; Broad request ('full preflight', 'list issues by severity', 'is this file good to go', or no specific attribute) → omit `scopes` and report EVERY finding the tool returned. Tool returns raw facts only — findings are pre-aggregated by issue tag with `display_name` and `affected_objects[]`. No severity in JSON. Agent classifies each finding per the SCOPE DISCIPLINE — PREFLIGHT SEVERITY policy in the system prompt. Each affected_objects[] entry contains uuid (when object-scoped), name, and issue-specific raw fields (e.g., effective_ppi, stroke_width, font_family). checks_skipped: optional array of checks that could not run due to suite errors or unavailability. Each entry has 'check' (tag) and 'reason'. IMPORTANT: an empty findings category is only trustworthy when checks_skipped contains no entry for that category. Final response (agent narrative): open with one sentence using `total_issues` from the summary (count of distinct issue types) and the output moment (e.g. '8 issues need attention before printing.'). Then emit up to 3 labelled sections in this order: **Critical Issues: N**, **Warnings: N**, and **Passed Checks** (no count — derived from absences of failed findings in scopes that were actually run; reference `checks_skipped` to avoid claiming a check passed when it was skipped). Skip **Critical Issues** or **Warnings** when N = 0. If Critical Issues and Warnings are both zero say 'Your file is production ready. No issues found.' and still include the Passed Checks section listing what was verified. Each finding (and each Passed Checks entry) is a single numbered line: N. {display_name} — {one-line action or consequence, or for Passed Checks: one-line confirmation of what passed}. No sub-lists. No bold heading per finding. No emojis. Restart numbering at 1 in Warnings and Passed Checks. Do NOT replace the numbered-list-of-findings with a single markdown table whose rows are the findings themselves; a per-finding affected-objects table as supplementary detail beneath a numbered finding line is OK, but the numbered line is required. Severity classification is principle-based (output moment + missing/render-breaking vs context-dependent) per the system prompt's PREFLIGHT SEVERITY policy — do not consult a static issue-to-tier table. Does not cover vision-only checks (contrast, visual alignment) or checks needing export-format context (transparency flattening). Use this for ANY readiness/verification request — prompts phrased with check / inspect / audit / verify / validate against document attributes (color mode, profile, bleed, resolution, units, artboard sizes, hidden or locked layers within export-range artboards, fonts, linked images, embedded images, text sizing/overset, spot colors, hairline strokes, overprint, transparency), as well as bare 'check this' / 'run a preflight' / 'production QA' / 'is it ready for print|export|share' / 'verify ... for print output'.

artboardIndex.description: Optional 1-based artboard index (1 = first artboard). When set, both artboard-level checks and per-object findings are restricted to art that intersects the target artboard. Omit to scan the entire document.

scopes.description: Optional list of check domains to run. Valid values: document, images, links, text, colors, objects. Omit or pass an empty array to run all domains. Example: [\"images\", \"links\"] runs only image-resolution and broken-link checks. Unknown values are silently ignored.

tools.name: RunPreflightChecks

tools.description: Rename one or more objects (including layers). IMPORTANT: Parameters are arrays, even for a single object. Example: uuids=['123'], newNames=['MyShape']. For batch: uuids=['123','456'], newNames=['Shape1','Shape2']. Arrays must have matching lengths. Response format: {success, details, uuids: [], success_count, fail_count}.

newNames.description: Array of new names, one per UUID (always use array, even for one object).

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to rename. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: RenameObject

tools.description: Select or deselect one or more art objects by UUID in Adobe Illustrator. Supports batch selection. Set select=false to deselect instead. BATCH PROCESSING: When selecting/deselecting multiple objects, pass array of UUIDs to process all in one call. Response format: {success, details, uuids: [], success_count, fail_count}.

deselectOthers.description: true to deselect all other objects first (before selecting the specified UUIDs)

select.description: true to select, false to deselect

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to select. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: SelectObjects

tools.description: Removes one or more objects (including layers) from the canvas by their UUIDs. When deleting layers, or when the UUIDs come from an earlier turn rather than a tool call in the current turn, call GetCanvasStructure first to confirm the UUIDs, locked state, and contents — document state may have changed. UUIDs obtained from a tool call in the current turn do not require re-inspection. Do not pass layer names. Deleting a group or layer also deletes all objects inside it. This tool does not delete artboards (use DeleteArtboard for that). Cannot delete the last remaining top-level layer. Pass uuids as an array even for a single object (e.g. uuids=[\"123\"]). Locked and hidden objects are skipped and reported in skipped_objects unless force=true. With force=true, locked and hidden objects are deleted regardless of their state; the containing layer's lock and visibility are not permanently changed.

force.description: Default false. When true, bypasses the locked/hidden skip check to allow deletion. Set to true only when the user explicitly names a locked or hidden target for deletion. Never set true for generic requests like 'delete all' or 'clean up'.

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects/layers to delete. For layers, first get layer UUIDs from GetCanvasStructure (not layer names). Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: DeleteObjects

tools.description: Creates copies of one or more objects by their UUIDs with optional positional offset. Offsets are in points with Y-down (positive offsetY moves down). Response format: {success, details, uuids: [new_copy_uuids], parent_name, parent_uuid, parent_type (of first duplicate's parent), failed_objects?: [{uuid, reason}, ...]}.

artName.description: Name to assign to the duplicated artwork (only applies when duplicating a single object)

offsetX.description: Horizontal offset in points to apply to each duplicate (0 = same position as original)

offsetY.description: Vertical offset in points to apply to each duplicate (0 = same position as original)

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to duplicate. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: DuplicateObjects

tools.description: Create a new empty group. Returns `uuid` of the created group. Position defaults to top of the layer stack (frontmost). IMPORTANT: Each new group is placed at the front, so creating multiple groups without explicit positioning reverses their visual stacking order. When creating multiple groups for restructuring, either create them in back-to-front order (background group first, foreground group last) or use position='below:<uuid>' to place each group at the correct depth relative to existing objects. To add objects to the group, use MoveObjectsToContainer with the returned group UUID.

artName.description: Name to assign to the group

parentID.description: UUID of a container (layer or group) to create inside. When provided, 'front'/'back' place at top/bottom inside this container. Ignored when position is 'above:<uuid>' or 'below:<uuid>'. Omit to create in the current layer.

position.description: Where to place in the z-order: 'front' (topmost, default), 'back' (bottommost), 'above:<uuid>' (above referenced object), 'below:<uuid>' (below referenced object). When parentID is provided, 'front'/'back' place inside that container. 'above:<uuid>'/'below:<uuid>' always place relative to the referenced object — parentID is ignored. When replacing an object (including placing a Firefly-edited version back), use 'above:<uuid-of-original>' to preserve its stacking position — and always call this tool BEFORE deleting the original; deleting first causes PlaceImage to fail with 'Reference object not found'.

tools.name: CreateGroup

tools.description: Relocates one or more objects into a new parent container at a specified position. Objects are always placed in their current visual z-order (front-to-back stacking from the artwork), regardless of the array order provided. To reorder objects after moving, use ArrangeArt. Position values: 'front' (topmost, default), 'back' (bottommost), 'above:<uuid>' (above the referenced object), 'below:<uuid>' (below the referenced object). Layers cannot be moved inside groups — only into other layers. Moving all children out of a group automatically removes that group; do not delete it afterward (layers are not auto-removed). Response format: {success, details, uuids: [], moved_count, failed_count, failed_objects?: [{uuid, reason}, ...], skipped_count, skipped_objects?: [{uuid, reason}, ...], auto_deleted_containers?: [uuid, ...]}. skipped_objects hit an inherent limitation and were not moved; do not retry them. auto_deleted_containers lists UUIDs of groups that were implicitly deleted because all their children were moved out — do NOT call DeleteObjects on these UUIDs.

parentID.description: UUID of the target container (layer or group). When provided with 'front'/'back', objects are placed inside this container. When omitted with 'front'/'back', objects are placed at the absolute top/bottom of the document. Ignored when position is 'above:<uuid>' or 'below:<uuid>'.

position.description: Where to place: 'front' (topmost, default), 'back' (bottommost), 'above:<uuid>' (above referenced object), 'below:<uuid>' (below referenced object). 'above:<uuid>'/'below:<uuid>' always place relative to the referenced object -- parentID is ignored.

uuids.description: List of UUIDs to move. The objects will be placed in their current visual z-order (matching the order from GetArtboardStructure/GetCanvasStructure), not the array order provided. Always pass an array, even for one object. IMPORTANT: Never split UUIDs into batched calls — pass all UUIDs for the same container in one call. Splitting corrupts z-order.

tools.name: MoveObjectsToContainer

tools.description: Creates a clipping mask group. The maskUuid object becomes the clipping path (defines the visible area). The clipUuids objects are the content that gets clipped. All objects are moved into a new group, with the clipping path on top. Returns `uuid` of the new clipping mask group.

artName.description: Name to assign to the clipping group

clipUuids.description: UUIDs of objects to be clipped (the content). Always pass an array, even for one object.

maskUuid.description: UUID of the path to use as the clipping mask (defines the visible area)

parentID.description: UUID of a container (layer or group) to create inside. When provided, 'front'/'back' place at top/bottom inside this container. Ignored when position is 'above:<uuid>' or 'below:<uuid>'. Omit to create in the current layer.

position.description: Where to place in the z-order: 'front' (topmost, default), 'back' (bottommost), 'above:<uuid>' (above referenced object), 'below:<uuid>' (below referenced object). When parentID is provided, 'front'/'back' place inside that container. 'above:<uuid>'/'below:<uuid>' always place relative to the referenced object — parentID is ignored. When replacing an object (including placing a Firefly-edited version back), use 'above:<uuid-of-original>' to preserve its stacking position — and always call this tool BEFORE deleting the original; deleting first causes PlaceImage to fail with 'Reference object not found'.

tools.name: CreateClippingMask

tools.description: Changes the z-order (stacking order) of objects within their current layer or group. When applied to a top-level layer UUID, reorders that layer in the document's layer stack. Operations: 'bring_to_front' moves to top within its container (or to the front of the layer stack for layers), 'send_to_back' moves to bottom, 'bring_forward' moves one step toward front, 'send_backward' moves one step toward back. To move objects between layers, use MoveObjectsToContainer. BATCH ORDERING: provide uuids in front-to-back order. The tool may process uuids in an operation-specific internal order to preserve intuitive front-to-back outcomes, and returns uuids in original input order. Response format: {success, details, uuids: [] (in original input order), success_count, fail_count, failed_objects?: [{uuid, reason}, ...]}.

uuids.description: UUIDs of objects to arrange. Provide uuids in front-to-back order (first UUID is frontmost). The tool may use operation-specific internal processing order to preserve intuitive front-to-back outcomes. Always pass an array, even for one object. IMPORTANT: Never split UUIDs into batched calls — pass all UUIDs for the same operation in one call. Splitting corrupts z-order.

tools.name: ArrangeArt

tools.description: Read available swatches from the active document's Swatches panel or any swatch library. Use whenever a swatch's name, group, or color is needed. Defaults to 'Document Swatches'; pass swatchLibraryName for a known preset library, or listLibraries=true to enumerate libraries. **When the library name is unknown, call with listLibraries=true first; never guess or infer library names.** Pass swatchName for an exact (caseless) lookup; omit to list every swatch in the chosen library. Results: { libraryName: { groupName: [...] } } — name strings on listings; entries become { name, color } objects when swatchName is set. Bulk listings cap at 100 names — for larger libraries (Toyo Color Finder, TRUMATCH, etc.) infer additional swatch names from the swatch naming convention and call again with swatchName. This does not report which swatches are actually used by artwork in the document; for that, inspect object fill/stroke appearance.

listLibraries.description: true to return the list of available swatch libraries instead of swatches (other params ignored). Default false.
