swatchLibraryName.description: Library to read swatches from. Defaults to 'Document Swatches' when omitted. Must be an exact library name — call with listLibraries=true first if the name is not already known. Never guess or infer library names.

swatchName.description: Swatch name to look up (caseless exact match) within the chosen library. Omit to list every swatch in the library.

tools.name: GetSwatches

tools.description: Style-preserving find and replace within a text frame. Replaced text inherits the original character styles. Occurrences using missing/substituted fonts, embedded glyph-subset fonts, or spanning mixed character styles are skipped by default (see skipped_occurrences and action_required). When the target font lacks glyphs for the replacement script, a system fallback font is applied automatically and reported in fallback_fonts_applied (array). If no fallback covers the script, render_warning is set and unfixable_occurrences lists which occurrence(s) are affected. Omit searchText to replace the entire frame content.

caseSensitive.description: When true (default), matching is case-sensitive. When false, matching ignores case (e.g. 'cafe' matches 'CAFE'). Accents are always significant.

forceReplace.description: When true, replace ALL occurrences even if they use missing (substituted) fonts, embedded glyph-subset fonts (subset is replaced with the system default), or span mixed character styles. Mixed-style matches inherit the FIRST character's style. Default false — such occurrences are skipped and reported so the user can decide. Only set to true after the user explicitly approves.

occurrences.description: 0-based indices of occurrences to replace (e.g. [0,2] replaces the 1st and 3rd match). Omit to replace all occurrences. An empty array is an error.

searchText.description: Text to find (case-sensitive by default). If wholeWord is false, typographic variants (curly quotes, em-dashes) are normalized to ASCII and retried as a fallback, but only when the exact text finds zero matches. Omit to replace the entire text frame content.

wholeWord.description: Whole-word matching. Default true — 'hand' will NOT match inside 'comprehand' or 'handful', but WILL match in 'hand-made' and 'hand's' (hyphen and apostrophe are word boundaries). Set false only when the user explicitly wants substring matching.

tools.name: ReplaceText

tools.description: Find every occurrence of one font in the active document and replace it with another, leaving other fonts in mixed-font text frames untouched. Operates document-wide. 'findFontFamily'/'findFontStyle' match only what's actually used in the document, never whether it's installed (so a substituted/missing font can still be found and replaced) — empty findFontStyle matches any style of the family. 'replaceFontFamily'/'replaceFontStyle' must be installed. Response reports success_count (text frames with at least one matching run), fail_count, and failed_objects ({uuid, reason}).

findFontFamily.description: Font family or PostScript name to find (e.g. 'Myriad Pro').

findFontStyle.description: Style variant of the font to find, e.g. 'Bold'. Leave empty to match any style of the family.

replaceFontFamily.description: Font family or PostScript name to replace with.

replaceFontStyle.description: Style variant to apply, e.g. 'Bold'. Leave empty when replaceFontFamily is a PostScript name.

tools.name: ReplaceFont

tools.description: Do NOT use this tool to CREATE or ADJUST alignment, distribution, or spacing between objects (see DistributeObjects/AlignObjects, which compute the correct offsets directly) -- fine for repositioning a group as a unit ('absolute' mode explicitly preserves existing spacing between the moved objects). Move or place one or more art objects. x and y are each optional; omit one to leave that axis unchanged. TWO MODES: (1) 'relative' (default): x/y are shift distances added to every object. Example: x=50, y=0 nudges objects 50pt right. (2) 'absolute': x/y set the top-left corner of the combined bounding box to that canvas position, preserving spacing between objects. Prefer 'absolute' when you have a target position. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down.

mode.description: How x/y are interpreted: 'relative' (default) shifts objects by x/y distances, 'absolute' places the combined bounding box top-left at (x,y).

uuids.description: UUIDs of the objects to move. Layer UUIDs are not supported. Always pass an array, even for one object.

x.description: Relative mode: horizontal shift in points (positive=right). Absolute mode: target left coordinate for the combined bounding box. Omit to preserve current horizontal position.

y.description: Relative mode: vertical shift in points (positive=down). Absolute mode: target top coordinate for the combined bounding box. Omit to preserve current vertical position.

tools.name: MoveObjects

tools.description: Rotate one or more art objects by a specified angle in degrees around the center of their combined bounding box. Example: angle=90 rotates 90 degrees counterclockwise, angle=-45 rotates 45 degrees clockwise.

angle.description: Angle to rotate in degrees (positive = counterclockwise)

uuids.description: UUIDs of the objects to rotate. Layer UUIDs are not supported. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: RotateObjects

tools.description: Scale one or more art objects around the center of their combined bounding box, preserving relative positions. MODES: 'factor' (default) sx/sy are multipliers (2=double, 0.5=half, 1=no change); 'absolute' sx/sy are target width/height in points — prefer 'absolute' when you have a target size. If the user names only ONE axis ('scale the width to 2x'), pass just that axis and OMIT the other - it scales uniformly (naming an axis picks which number is given, it does NOT freeze the other). Set maintainAspectRatio=false (needs both sx and sy) when the user gives explicit values for BOTH axes at an unequal ratio ('4in wide and 6in tall', '2x wide and 1.5x tall'), OR uses distortion words (stretch/squash/distort/ignore aspect ratio), OR pins an axis (only/just/'leave the height'). Otherwise keep the default true. Not for use during cleanup/organization tasks - only when the user explicitly requests a visual change.

maintainAspectRatio.description: Default true (see tool description for when to set false). With both sx and sy given, applies one uniform scale to both axes: the smaller magnitude of sx/sy in factor mode (per-axis sign kept, so a mirror stays mirrored), or the smaller sx/sy-to-current-size ratio in absolute mode (fits within the target). False applies sx and sy exactly/independently (may distort) and requires both sx and sy - if only one axis is given, this must stay true (the default); setting it false with a single axis is rejected as invalid.

mode.description: 'factor' (default): sx/sy are multipliers. 'absolute': sx/sy are target dimensions in points.

sx.description: Horizontal factor (factor mode) or target width in points (absolute mode). Omit to derive from sy, preserving proportions.

sy.description: Vertical factor (factor mode) or target height in points (absolute mode). Omit to derive from sx, preserving proportions.

uuids.description: UUIDs of the objects to scale. Layer UUIDs are not supported. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: ScaleObjects
